# Actual depth regions: deficit and erosion fail BM concavity

Take n=d=1 and C=[-1,1] x [-1,1], with the normalized length measure
on the three integer fibers. Fix t=1/12 and let D_t be its ordinary
ambient Tukey depth region.

At either endpoint integer fiber z=-1 or z=1, the depth at (z,x) is

    (1-|x|)/6, -1<=x<=1.                                  (1)

The own interval proves the lower bound: any halfspace containing the
point cuts at least 1-|x| units from it. For the upper bound, take the
smaller endpoint cap in that interval and use a sufficiently large
integer-coordinate normal to exclude the other two bounded fibers.
This produces a closed oblique ambient halfspace with exactly the
claimed mass.

At the middle integer fiber z=0, the depth is

    (1-|x|)/2.                                            (2)

The horizontal smaller cap proves the upper bound. For the lower
bound, by reflection take x>=0. For a positive continuous normal,
scaled to one, the two outer fiber thresholds are x+a and x-a.
Their cap-length sum is at least 2(1-x). Indeed it equals this until
one threshold reaches an interval endpoint, and then cannot fall
below this value; equivalently inspect the three intervals
|a|<=1-x, 1-x<=|a|<=1+x, and |a|>=1+x. The middle cap contributes
1-x, for a total at least 3(1-x). For the opposite continuous normal,
the two outer cap lengths sum to at least two and the middle length
is 1+x, giving at least 3+x>=3(1-x). Purely integer normals include
the full middle fiber and at least one outer fiber and hence have
mass at least 2/3. This proves (2).

Consequently the actual depth-region sections are

    (D_t)_(-1)=(D_t)_1=[-1/2,1/2],
    (D_t)_0=[-5/6,5/6].                                  (3)

The removed-volume function at these three indices equals

    vol(C_(-1))-vol((D_t)_(-1))=1,
    vol(C_0)-vol((D_t)_0)=1/3,
    vol(C_1)-vol((D_t)_1)=1.

It is not even quasiconcave on the integer line, since its midpoint
value is smaller than both endpoint values. No positive-power BM
concavity can hold for these deficits.

The Minkowski erosions have exactly the same lengths:

    C_(-1) minus_erosion (D_t)_(-1)=[-1/2,1/2],
    C_0 minus_erosion (D_t)_0=[-1/6,1/6],
    C_1 minus_erosion (D_t)_1=[-1/2,1/2].

Thus even the set-valued midpoint inclusion fails for erosion: the
Minkowski average of the two endpoint erosion intervals is [-1/2,1/2],
which is not contained in the middle erosion interval.

This is different from the ordinary fiberwise Minkowski sum with the
negative depth section. The lengths of C_z+(-(D_t)_z) are 3,11/3,3,
which do satisfy the ordinary concavity expected from the convex
fiber-product construction. That valid statement does not transfer
to set-theoretic removal or erosion.
